title: SWEDEN'S 2026 ELECTION: FIRST VOTE ON NATO ERA AFTER 200 YEARS OF NEUTRALITY
excerpt: Sweden's upcoming election marks the first vote since abandoning 200 years of military non-alignment. Denmark faces snap election amid Greenland sovereignty tensions. Finland proposes lifting nuclear weapons ban.
body: Sweden's 2026 election will be the first test of voter sentiment since abandoning 200 years of military non-alignment to join NATO. The Riksdag's 269-349 vote approving NATO accession in 2024 followed Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion. Meanwhile, Denmark's snap election on March 24 centers on sovereignty concerns following U.S. interest in purchasing Greenland. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats lead polls with a red bloc at 48.7%. Finland's government proposes amending the 1987 Nuclear Energy Act to lift prohibitions on nuclear weapons for defense, drawing Kremlin warnings of countermeasures.
keywords: Sweden NATO, Denmark election, Finland nuclear, Ireland SNA, Greenland sovereignty
sources: Riksdag records; Voxmeter polling; Kremlin statements; Irish Department of Education
